provisions.title: Cleartext Transmission of Sensitive Information
provisions.text: The product transmits sensitive or security-critical data in cleartext in a communication channel that can be sniffed by unauthorized actors.

provisions.title: Broken Object Level Authorization
provisions.text: Every API endpoint that receives an ID of an object, and performs any action on the object, should implement object-level authorization checks. The checks should validate that the logged-in user has permissions to perform the requested action on the requested object.

provisions.title: Protection of action taken in good faith
provisions.text: No suit, prosecution or other legal proceedings shall lie against the Central Government, the Board, its Chairperson and any Member, officer or employee thereof for anything which is done or intended to be done in good faith under the provisions of this Act or the rules made thereunder.

value.reason: In terraform/networking.tf (lines 157-166), the aws_lb_listener 'http' listens on port 80 with protocol HTTP. Its default_action is 'forward' straight to the juice_shop target group. It does not redirect to HTTPS, and no TLS is set on it. This matches the positive example and differs from the negative one, which uses a 301 redirect to HTTPS. Personal data behind this listener therefore travels over the network in cleartext. The data model in models/address.ts links address records to users through UserId, so this traffic includes personal profile and address data. The exposure is marked Internal-Restricted, but the evidence doesn't show that the load balancer is internal-only or that traffic is encrypted some other way. An unencrypted channel carrying personal data is cleartext transmission (CWE-319) and falls short of the encryption-based security safeguards required under DPDP Rule 6(1)(a).
